coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P11
names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P11
P11 -- landscaped median strip connecting Mission Bay Circle to P11A
record.summary: A tree-lined median strip running within the road right-of-way, connecting the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout east to the P11A half-circle island; per Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery (OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map labels the strip 'P11' but does not describe it), an already-landscaped median, hand-traced from satellite imagery and fit to a rotated rectangle. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P11/11A' together among the parcels SF Recreation and Parks will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels); that presentation is a plan and does not say whether the strip was built. SF Recreation and Parks' April 2025 timeline says "P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)". The City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement lists P11 among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and says P10, P11 and P11A 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works); the draft says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay Parks, but not who built this parcel, and no signed text of the agreement was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- satellite trace of an outline drawn by Pier & Point, idealized to a fitted rectangle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. Not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this is a real median strip that sits entirely within the paved road right-of-way by design -- trimming it against the generic street buffer would remove it entirely, not correct a mispositioning. An accepted exception. An earlier version of this record placed P11 at a different, already-tracked Mission Bay Commons site near Illinois St, inferred only from a source note that gave build years for P11, P16 and P17 as a group; it was moved to this median strip on 2026-09-19.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery, following an outline Pier & Point marked on a screenshot and transferred onto the map, then fit to an idealized road-aligned rectangle based on Pier & Point's description of the real shape.

milestones.text: SF Recreation and Parks' Mission Bay Parks Community Meeting #3 presentation (April 29, 2025), Timeline slide, lists "P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)" (an event year given in a later retrospective timeline; no month, and the slide does not describe the parcel). OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map labels the thin strip between Mission Bay Circle and P11A "P11", which is why that entry is read as this strip

open_questions: OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map labels this strip "P11", and SF Recreation and Parks' April 2025 timeline says "P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)"; neither gives a month or describes the strip. OCII's September 2023 presentation is a plan (RPD "will manage" P11/11A) and does not itself say the strip was built.

OCII's November 2024 CAC update lists "Mission Bay Commons (P11, P12, P13, P15, P16, P17)" as one group of parks; its map puts the "P11" label at the Mission Bay Circle roundabout, where the December 2019 Land Use Map also draws P11, and shows only P12-P15 as current interim use or pilot sites.

Who built and who holds it: the City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement (recital D) lists P10, P11 and P11A among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and section 5(j) says they 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works), with any CFD funds used by RPD to maintain them on PW's behalf or passed to PW. Recital C says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay parks; no source read says who built these three parcels. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo says the Board would need to vacate the public right-of-way status on the park parcels, and the Board's December 5, 2023 resolution (File 231132) approved the agreement and said Port and RPD expected to seek the jurisdictional transfer by a separate ordinance in early 2024. No signed agreement, transfer ordinance or later source on these three parcels was found, so Public Works is the holder per the draft only.

The shape of P11 rests on Pier & Point's judgment: SF Rec & Park's April 2025 timeline lists 'P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)' without describing the parcel, and OCII's November 2024 CAC update groups P11 with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 as 'Mission Bay Commons'. OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map draws the 'P11' label on a thin strip just east of Mission Bay Circle, where this strip is. Whether P11 is only this 4.8 m median or a larger Commons segment has not been settled.

record.notes: Thin landscaped median strip with a row of trees, connecting the Mission Bay Circle roundabout to the P11A median island. The 'landscaped' and 'row of trees' description is Pier & Point's own reading of its satellite trace; no document read describes it. A September 2023 draft Mission Bay parks maintenance agreement, in a section headed 'Median Strip and Traffic Circle in P10 and P11/11A', says P10, P11 and P11A are not being accepted by Recreation and Parks and will remain public rights of way under Public Works (a draft, so not necessarily the signed text).
